data.title: Natural Grocers outlines 2%-3% comp growth and $2.03-$2.10 EPS for fiscal 2027 while expanding to 7-9 new stores
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage (NGVC) Q4 fiscal 2026

Management View

  • "Fiscal 2026 marked our 23rd consecutive year of positive comparable store sales growth" and "daily average comparable store sales growth accelerated sequentially in each of the last two quarters, reaching 2.5% in the fourth quarter" (Chairman & Co-President Kemper Isely).
  • "{N}power penetration reached 85% of net sales in the fourth quarter, up from 82% a year ago" and management said it supports "relevant and personalized offers" and reinforces "Always Affordable pricing" and the "Even More Affordable campaign" (Chairman & Co-President Isely).
  • "Fiscal 2026 marked the first year of our accelerated unit growth strategy, during which we opened 7 stores and entered our 22nd state" and "for fiscal 2027, we plan to open 7 to 9 new stores" (Chairman & Co-President Isely).
  • "We launched DoorDash delivery across all stores" with "in-store prices," "integrated {N}power rewards into DoorDash," and later "completed the rollout of curbside pickup at all our stores through Instacart"; management added, "Early results from our expanded e-commerce offering are encouraging" (Chairman & Co-President Isely).
  • "Our Natural Grocers brand products continue to deliver strong growth" and "in the fourth quarter, they represented 9.3% of total sales, up from 8.8% a year ago" (Chairman & Co-President Isely).
  • "Fourth quarter results reflected improved sales momentum and disciplined expense management, partially offset by lower gross margin and higher pre-opening expenses" (Chief Financial Officer Richard Hallé).

Outlook

  • "We expect to open 7 to 9 new stores" and "deliver daily average comparable store sales growth between 2% and 3%" and "generate diluted earnings per share between $2.03 and $2.10" in fiscal 2027 (Chief Financial Officer Hallé).
  • "We expect the pace of new store openings to be weighted towards the back half of fiscal 2027" and "for comparable store sales, we expect growth to improve modestly as the year progresses" (Chief Financial Officer Hallé).
  • "We expect full-year gross margin to be relatively flat year-over-year, with potential first half pressure related to recent shrink and freight trends" (Chief Financial Officer Hallé).
  • "Pre-opening expenses are expected to be $3.5 to $4 million" and "invest $55 to $60 million in capital expenditures" (Chief Financial Officer Hallé).
  • Versus the prior quarter’s fiscal 2026 framework, management’s focus shifted from refining fiscal 2026 targets (including "daily average comparable store sales growth between 1.5% and 2%" and "diluted earnings per share between $2.07 and $2.11") to establishing fiscal 2027 targets (Chief Financial Officer Hallé, Q3 transcript; Chief Financial Officer Hallé, Q4 transcript).

Financial Results

  • "Net sales were $347.5 million" and "daily average comparable store sales increased 2.5%" in Q4; management also said comparable sales were "6.7%" on a two-year basis (Chief Financial Officer Hallé).
  • "Gross margin decreased 21 basis points to 29.2%" and management attributed it to "higher merchandise inventory shrink and freight costs" (Chief Financial Officer Hallé).
  • "Fourth quarter net income was $11.3 million" and "diluted earnings per share was $0.48, compared to $0.51 in the prior year period"; "Adjusted EBITDA increased 2.2% to $24.9 million" (Chief Financial Officer Hallé).
  • Management said, "Compared to our August outlook, comparable store sales were in line with the low end of our range, while diluted earnings per share were below the range, primarily driven by lower gross margin" (Chief Financial Officer Hallé).
  • For fiscal 2026, "net sales increased 1.8% to $1.36 billion," "gross margin declined 31 basis points" (with the driver "higher merchandise inventory shrink"), and "diluted earnings per share increased 1.5% to $2.03" (Chief Financial Officer Hallé).
  • Liquidity and cash flow included "$32.1 million in cash and cash equivalents," "free cash flow of $33.9 million," and "no outstanding credit facility borrowings" (Chief Financial Officer Hallé).

Q&A

  • Aaron Grey, Alliance Global Partners: "early indicators from the DoorDash initiative" and how much lift is embedded in comp guidance; Chief Financial Officer Hallé: "What we've seen to date is really good performance" and "we are expecting that to create a lift as we move through the second half of the year" while adding, "we're not providing a component of our comps related to e-commerce".
  • Aaron Grey, Alliance Global Partners: gross margin drivers including "freight" and whether "shrink" is lasting longer; Chief Financial Officer Hallé: "on freight, it's having an impact" and "On shrink... for us, it's very much an operational issue" with a focus on "inventory controls" and "accountability in the store," and "it will normalize as we march into the second half".
  • Yanjun Liu, BofA Securities: "promotional or pricing environment" and "signs of intensifying competition"; Chairman & Co-President Isely: "we haven't really seen an uptick in competition" and "I don't think that really has increased at all either".
  • Yanjun Liu, BofA Securities: whether "Even More Affordable" needs further investment given negative transactions; Chairman & Co-President Isely: "I think the Even More Affordable campaign is working very well" and "it's drawn in new customers".

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analyst tone was neutral-to-slightly negative, pressing on embedded e-commerce lift, gross margin durability, and shrink persistence (e.g., "how much of a lift you're embedding" and "has that ended up being an impact longer than you expected") (Aaron Grey, Alliance Global Partners; Chief Financial Officer Hallé responses).
  • Management tone was slightly positive in prepared remarks and more operationally detailed in Q&A; confidence language included "we remain confident" and "Early results... are encouraging," while margin commentary acknowledged pressure ("potential first half pressure") (Chairman & Co-President Isely; Chief Financial Officer Hallé).
  • Versus the prior quarter, the discussion on shrink and freight remained prominent, but Q4 leaned more on e-commerce rollout completion and fiscal 2027 framing; Q3 also described a "challenging consumer environment" and highlighted an "initial phase" DoorDash launch (Chairman & Co-President Isely, Q3 transcript; Chairman & Co-President Isely, Q4 transcript).

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • Q4 emphasized accelerating comps ("reaching 2.5% in the fourth quarter") and full deployment of omnichannel tools (DoorDash across all stores; curbside pickup rollout complete), while Q3 emphasized sequential comp improvement to "1.2%" and early-stage e-commerce expansion plans (Chairman & Co-President Isely, Q3 transcript; Chairman & Co-President Isely, Q4 transcript).
  • Q4 guidance introduced fiscal 2027 targets ("2% and 3%" comps; EPS "between $2.03 and $2.10"; capex "$55 to $60 million"), whereas Q3 refined fiscal 2026 ranges and cited a tactical calendar impact ("close stores on Labor Day") (Chief Financial Officer Hallé, Q3 transcript; Chief Financial Officer Hallé, Q4 transcript).
  • Analyst focus narrowed in Q4 to e-commerce lift and margin drivers, compared with Q3’s broader set including loyalty program differentiation and consumer macro discussion (Alliance Global Partners; R5 Capital; BofA Securities).

Risks and Concerns

  • Margin headwinds were tied to "higher merchandise inventory shrink and freight costs" and management warned of "potential first half pressure" in fiscal 2027 (Chief Financial Officer Hallé).
  • Management framed shrink as process-driven: "very much an operational issue" with initiatives focused on "inventory controls" and "accountability" (Chief Financial Officer Hallé).
  • Store-growth investment was explicitly described as earnings pressure: fiscal 2027 EPS includes "incremental year-over-year expenses related to new stores of approximately $0.12" and pre-opening expense guidance of "$3.5 to $4 million" (Chief Financial Officer Hallé).

Final Takeaway

Management framed Q4 as a quarter of improving sales momentum alongside ongoing gross margin pressure from shrink and freight, while positioning fiscal 2027 around continued unit expansion (7 to 9 stores), moderated comp growth expectations (2% to 3%), and investments in e-commerce and productivity initiatives, with profitability guided to $2.03 to $2.10 in diluted EPS and gross margin expected to be relatively flat year-over-year despite first-half pressure.

data.title: Tsakos Energy Navigation plans Singapore dual listing in Q1 while earmarking $150M for preferred and common repurchases
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Tsakos Energy Navigation (TEN) Q3 2026

Management View

  • "Another set of brilliant results on the back, of course, of a very strong market, but also because of the best-in-class operating performance of TEN" (Chairman Efstratios-Georgios Arapoglou). "We continue to generate and maintain a very healthy buffer of cash, which allows us to make use of opportunities, renew our fleet, offer healthy increases in dividends and potentially repaying or redeeming some of our preferred obligations as well as potentially buy back stock." He added: "The total of $3.6 billion of committed future earnings is the best evidence of this successful path."

  • "It's a very nice occasion to report another record period, $850 million and growing revenues, $403 million of net income" (CEO Nikolas Tsakos). He tied near-term operating decisions to security conditions: "We are learning to live with these new circumstances. We are taking advantage of the very high rates without any risk to our seafarers, our ships and our cargoes." He also flagged pipeline announcements: "Very soon, I think we will be announcing sometime in December further new strategic alliances and business in the segments of deep sea and gas."

  • "We were pioneers of the New York Stock Exchange in 2002. And I believe that the future lies...in the East" (CEO Tsakos). On capital markets strategy: "We are...discussing closely with SGX, the dual listing of TEN shares" and said this could "provide with a time difference a 24-hour trading platform."

  • "During the third quarter, we took delivery of the DP Suezmax shuttle tanker Anfield...The vessel commenced a 10-year employment to a U.S. oil major" (President/COO George Saroglou). He also framed the fleet’s contract mix: "25 vessels or 41% of the operating fleet has market exposure...while 49 of the vessels or 80% of the fleet is in secured revenue contracts."

  • "Gross revenues during the first 9 months of 2026 increased to $851 million" and "the net income generated by the company...reached $403 million" (CFO Harrys Kosmatos). He added: "Cash balances at the end of September 2026 stood at $534 million" and highlighted capital return: "the company's commitment to returning capital to shareholders" (CFO Kosmatos).

Outlook

  • "It is a first quarter event" for the Singapore listing, and "for sure, we will not be raising any equity. It will be just a direct quotation" (CEO Tsakos).

  • "By the time we come to New York for Capital Link, we will be able to have...all the news signed and sealed" regarding deepwater/gas initiatives (CEO Tsakos), after earlier noting the company was discussing "at least...2 vessels" with "anywhere between 7 and 10 years employment" in the DP segment.

  • "The special component, if any, will be added on the middle of July payment of the second semi-annual" (CEO Tsakos). He tied potential timing to market/sales conditions: "If the market continues to move the way it does and if the sales that we have in line...will be successful, we could have that special sometime in July."

Financial Results

  • "The resulting gross revenues...touched $300 million" in Q3 2026 and "net income for the third quarter of 2026...climbed to $174.5 million" (CFO Kosmatos). He also stated: "In terms of EPS...$5.57 for this year's third quarter" and "the company generated $185 million of adjusted EBITDA" in Q3.

  • "Operating income for the third quarter of 2026 reached $194 million...inclusive of a $56 million...capital gains" (CFO Kosmatos). He also said Q3 "fleet utilization remained nonetheless high at 93.5%" despite "7 vessels in dry dock."

  • "TEN's financial obligations...were $2.2 billion" at September 2026, while "corresponding interest and finance costs...settled to $65.7 million" for the first nine months (CFO Kosmatos).

Q&A

  • Omar Nokta, Clarksons: Asked if a 5-year VLCC time charter at "$125,000" was realistic; CEO Tsakos: "I think $100,000 has been done...Even $105,000 is acceptable rate."

  • Omar Nokta, Clarksons: Asked timing/structure of Singapore listing and whether it includes a capital raise; CEO Tsakos: "It is a first quarter event" and "we will not be raising any equity. It will be just a direct quotation."

  • Charles Fratt, Alliance Global Partners: Pressed for details on "deep water or gas-oriented investments"; CEO Tsakos: "we are in very close discussions with major end users" and referenced "at least...2 vessels" with "anywhere between 7 and 10 years employment" and said news could be ready by Capital Link.

  • Charles Fratt, Alliance Global Partners: Asked if profit-sharing revenue math was correct and Q4 outlook; CFO Kosmatos: "for the third quarter, it's $57.7 million" and CEO Tsakos: "I believe it's similar to the third quarter." CFO Kosmatos added: "we do not have any vessels on profit share that have its contract expiring before year-end."

  • Charles Fratt, Alliance Global Partners: Asked whether asset sales closed in Q3 and about buybacks; CFO Kosmatos: "Nothing yet in Q4" and confirmed the Q3 closings. On buybacks: "the announcement was...a $150 million like preferred and common stock buyback" and "the intention...would be to take" Series E "out...to redeem it at par."

  • Climent Molins, Value Investor's Edge: Asked why operating expenses rose and whether it was one-off; President/COO Saroglou: "We had a number of vessels that were repositioning" and "it was...a necessary evil," adding the company aims for "approximately 1/3 of the fleet in spot-related charters and the rest in longer-term employment."

  • Climent Molins, Value Investor's Edge: Asked about a special dividend; CEO Tsakos: "the special component, if any, will be added on the middle of July" and linked it to market conditions and asset sales.

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analyst tone was slightly skeptical on strategy and cost drivers, with direct pushes on feasibility and timing (e.g., "Is that a realistic rate you think in this environment?" and "why did operating expenses increase so significantly quarter-over-quarter?").

  • Management tone was confident in market conditions and capital actions, while emphasizing risk controls: "We are taking advantage of the very high rates without any risk to our seafarers" (CEO Tsakos) and "Our company continues to avoid the Strait of Hormuz" (President/COO Saroglou).

  • Versus the prior quarter, the current call introduced more concrete near-term catalysts ("It is a first quarter event" for SGX; "a $150 million...buyback") alongside continued geopolitical caution.

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • The current call elevated the capital markets narrative, with the Board citing "the initiative to explore a secondary listing in Singapore" (Chairman Arapoglou), while the prior quarter focused more on dividend framing and long-term charter appetite.

  • Backlog language increased modestly, from "approximately $3.5 billion" previously to "$3.6 billion of committed future earnings" (Chairman Arapoglou).

  • Capital return communication shifted from discussing potential preferred redemption/dividend increases in principle to detailing a buyback plan and redemption timing: "a $150 million...buyback" and Series E "becomes redeemable at the end of May next year" (CFO Kosmatos).

  • Operational/geopolitical messaging remained central, but Q3 added specific security updates and avoidance behavior, including "oil flows have recovered to around 80% of the pre-war levels" and "Our company continues to avoid the Strait of Hormuz" (President/COO Saroglou).

Risks and Concerns

  • "The ongoing conflict in the Middle East, the Red Sea and the war in Ukraine continue to disrupt oil and tanker markets" (President/COO Saroglou), and "attacks that continue on tankers crossing the Strait of Hormuz" remained a focal risk; mitigation was explicit: "Our company continues to avoid the Strait of Hormuz."

  • Costs and utilization pressure from fleet moves were acknowledged in Q&A: "repositioning" created "a cost" and was described as "a necessary evil" to move ships to "more lucrative...regions" (President/COO Saroglou).

Final Takeaway

Management described Q3 2026 as another record period supported by tanker market strength, with $3.6B of committed future earnings and a stated focus on locking in term coverage while keeping spot/profit-share upside. Executives emphasized operational caution amid conflict-driven volatility, including continued avoidance of the Strait of Hormuz, while pointing to near-term strategic catalysts: a planned SGX dual listing targeted for Q1 with no equity raise, and December/early-December timing for announcements around deepwater/DP and gas-related alliances. Capital returns featured prominently through a $150M preferred/common repurchase authorization and discussion of redeeming the Series E preferred at par when it becomes redeemable, alongside dividend language that included a doubled first 2027 semiannual payment and the possibility of a special component tied to July, contingent on market conditions and asset sales.

data.title: Keysight projects 20% fiscal 2027 revenue growth as it guides Q1 revenue to $2.040B-$2.060B
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Keysight Technologies (KEYS) Q4 fiscal 2026

Management View

  • "Fiscal 2026 was the strongest year in Keysight's history," said CEO Satish Dhanasekaran, adding, "We delivered a record fourth quarter, exceeding the high end of our guidance with orders up 53% and revenue up 41%."
  • Dhanasekaran tied demand to AI infrastructure, saying, "Wireline delivered record orders again this quarter" and describing customer activity spanning "silicon design through system emulation into high-value manufacturing."
  • On capital planning and supply, Dhanasekaran said the company "initiated strategic actions to scale our operations" including "broadening our supply base, building longer-term partnerships and adding manufacturing capacity."
  • Dhanasekaran announced a CFO transition: "Next month, Jason Kary will succeed Neil as Keysight's CFO," while recognizing "over 13 years" of contributions from outgoing CFO Neil Dougherty.
  • "Keysight delivered outstanding results in fiscal 2026," said CFO Neil Dougherty, highlighting "nearly $1.2 billion in R&D" and "repurchasing $667 million of Keysight stock" during the year.

Outlook

  • CFO Neil Dougherty guided Q1 fiscal 2027 revenue "in the range of $2.040 billion to $2.060 billion" vs. analysts’ $1,976,808,810, and guided Q1 EPS "in the range of $3.63 to $3.69" vs. analysts’ $3.25.
  • CEO Satish Dhanasekaran set a full-year framework: "Based on our visibility into demand and supply through the first half of the year, our base case for fiscal 2027 is 20% revenue growth."
  • Dougherty flagged a margin headwind: "we expect continued stability albeit without the onetime tailwind of 110 basis points that occurred in fiscal 2026 from the IEEPA tariff refunds," and added, "We expect capital expenditures to be approximately $275 million" and "a 14% non-GAAP effective tax rate."
  • Compared with the prior quarter’s outlook raise for fiscal 2026, management’s current commentary shifted to positioning: Dhanasekaran said, "we took a long-term view of supply" and framed fiscal 2027 around "record backlog" and "robust pipeline."

Financial Results

  • Q4 revenue was $1.994 billion vs. analysts’ $1,949,522,980 and Q4 EPS was $3.61 vs. analysts’ $3.38.
  • CFO Neil Dougherty reported Q4 profitability and costs: "Gross margin was 69%, and operating expenses were $662 million" and "Operating margin was 35.8%."
  • Dougherty reported cash and buybacks: "We ended the quarter with $2.916 billion in cash and cash equivalents" and "repurchased approximately 450,000 shares... for a total consideration of $150 million," with "$833 million remaining" on authorization.
  • On acquisitions, Dougherty said, "on a run rate basis, we have now realized the full $100 million of cost synergies" and that acquired businesses moved "from a collective operating margin of 11% in the first quarter to 32% by the fourth quarter."

Q&A

  • Mark Delaney, Goldman Sachs: asked about confidence in "20%" given better first-half visibility; CEO Dhanasekaran responded, "20% base case reflects... improved visibility... momentum in demand... steady progress on the supply chain" and added, "we remain confident in our ability to deliver and outperform in '27."
  • Mark Delaney, Goldman Sachs: asked when supply meets demand; Dhanasekaran said, "it's quite similar to where we were 3 months ago" and added, "our supply chain team is taking an 18-month view of supply."
  • Timothy Long, Barclays: asked what’s driving AI wireline acceleration; Dhanasekaran said, "our bookings in the AI business has been roughly 2.5x" year-over-year and "we have nearly doubled the amount of customers" in that business.
  • Timothy Long, Barclays: asked about incremental margins; CFO Dougherty said 2026 operating leverage was "approximately 50%" (adjusted) and for 2027 "somewhere in the mid- to upper 40s" would align.
  • Meta Marshall, Morgan Stanley: asked about a widening orders vs. revenue gap and 6G reflections; Dhanasekaran pointed to broad demand drivers and said, "I'm confident" in execution, while CSG President Kailash Narayanan added, "Our 6G business doubled year-over-year" and cited the "L.A. Olympics 2028 technology showcasing."
  • Andrew Spinola, UBS: asked about Q1 seasonality and supply de-constraints timing; CFO Dougherty said the base case is a "mid-single-digit sequential decline" in orders, and CEO Dhanasekaran said de-constraining "is a moving target" but "we remain confident" in the fiscal-year base case.
  • Adrienne Colby, Citi: asked about defense tech start-ups and EISG leadership; Dhanasekaran said solutions are "highly relevant" and "we already have sales teams," and on reporting lines said, "The EISG business... will report to Kailash."
  • Joseph Cardoso, JPMorgan: asked about pricing power and optical/CPO/NPO timing; Dhanasekaran said pricing is "proportional to the value delivered" and added, "we view this transition as well underway" with "a bigger inflection in '28" and "meaningful movements... in 2027."
  • Matthew Niknam, Truist: asked about backlog assumptions and quantifying AI revenue; CFO Dougherty said backlog extension was "$200 million to $300 million" tied to supply constraints, while Dhanasekaran said, "it's easier for us to quantify AI orders or bookings."
  • David Ridley-Lane, BofA: asked about non-AI growth math and recent order pattern changes; CFO Dougherty said, "I haven't done that math," and Dhanasekaran said, "No, no, none that we discern."
  • Quinn Fredrickson, Baird: asked whether constraints broadened and about share gains; CFO Dougherty said constraints are "heavily concentrated within a dozen to 2 dozen SKUs" tied to AI, and Dhanasekaran said, "We're really confident" and sales SVP Sung Yoon added, "our pipeline... stands at an all-time high" and "Customers are moving from quotations to PO faster."

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analysts’ tone was slightly skeptical, pressing on sustainability and constraints (e.g., Delaney asked if "the second half is a little bit more uncertain," and Spinola asked if de-constraint timing "changed in any way").
  • Management’s tone was confident and execution-focused in both prepared remarks and Q&A, with repeated assurance (e.g., CEO Dhanasekaran: "we remain confident"; CFO Dougherty: "we do expect to outperform the 40% long-term target").
  • Versus the prior quarter’s emphasis on raising near-term guidance, the current call leaned more on durability and scaling capacity, with Dhanasekaran reiterating an "18-month view" of supply and a "base case" for fiscal 2027.

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • The current quarter introduced a leadership change, with Dhanasekaran stating, "Jason Kary will succeed Neil as Keysight's CFO," while the prior quarter focused on "raising our outlook for Q4 and for the full fiscal year."
  • Guidance language shifted from Q3’s raised Q4 and FY2026 framework to a FY2027 baseline: Dhanasekaran moved from "strong setup as we enter fiscal '27" (Q3) to "our base case... is 20% revenue growth" (Q4).
  • Supply constraints remained central, but commentary evolved from Q3’s "supply chain will remain a governor" to Q4’s "moving target" and continued "steady progress" through fiscal 2027.
  • Analysts maintained recurring themes quarter-to-quarter: AI wireline sustainability, backlog/orders vs. revenue conversion, and supply-chain limits.

Risks and Concerns

  • Supply limitations remained explicit, with CFO Dougherty saying, "demand continues to stay ahead of our ability to ship" and describing constraints concentrated in "a dozen to 2 dozen SKUs" tied to AI.
  • Margin normalization risk was flagged by Dougherty: "without the onetime tailwind" from "IEEPA tariff refunds."

Final Takeaway

Management described fiscal 2026 as a record year and positioned fiscal 2027 around a 20% revenue-growth base case supported by record backlog, an all-time-high pipeline, and ongoing capacity actions to address supply constraints that remain concentrated in AI-related components. Leadership changes were highlighted with Jason Kary set to become CFO, while management maintained that AI infrastructure demand (including optical transitions and system emulation) and early 6G traction are expanding the company’s opportunity set into 2027 and beyond, alongside continued focus on operating leverage and capital discipline.

data.title: Intuit expects FY2027 revenue growth of 8%-9% as it plans Mailchimp sale and outlines Q2 EPS of $3.17-$3.22
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: Intuit (INTU) Q1 fiscal 2027

Management view

  • "We delivered Q1 revenue growth of 12% with revenue, operating income and earnings per share above the top end of the guidance," said CEO Sasan Goodarzi.
  • "We recently signed 3 more partnerships with Meta, Microsoft and SpaceXSI," CEO Goodarzi said, adding that QuickBooks is available through Claude, ChatGPT and Perplexity, and that TurboTax and Credit Karma are available inside Claude and ChatGPT.
  • CEO Goodarzi said Intuit is also expanding mid-market capabilities and "expanding our platform with the acquisition of Sequence, an AI-native revenue management platform that automates the entire quote-to-revenue process."
  • CEO Goodarzi announced a portfolio shift: "We have signed an agreement to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons," and said "Selling Mailchimp sharpens our focus" on AI-native lead-to-cash capabilities inside QuickBooks.
  • "Our results for the first quarter of fiscal 2027 include revenue of $4.4 billion, up 12%; GAAP operating income of $0.9 billion, up 63%; non-GAAP operating income of $1 billion, up 46%," said CFO Sandeep Aujla.

Outlook

  • "All guidance for both next quarter and the fiscal year does not include any impact from pending sale of Mailchimp, which we expect to close in early calendar year 2027," CFO Aujla said.
  • "We expect total company revenue growth of 6% to 7%," CFO Aujla said for Q2, including "GAAP earnings per share of $2.55 to $2.60 and non-GAAP earnings per share of $3.17 to $3.22."
  • For FY2027, CFO Aujla said Intuit updated its revenue outlook due to Credit Karma: "Full year guidance now includes total company revenue of $23.081 billion to $23.365 billion or growth of 8% to 9%," and "We now expect Consumer segment revenue growth of 2% to 4%."
  • CFO Aujla described tax pricing and timing impacts on Q2: "We expect these actions to lower tax ARPC in fiscal 2027 with greater impact in Q2" and said moving refund transfer processing in-house "will shift approximately $30 million from Q2 to Q3."

Financial results

  • CFO Aujla reported profitability and EPS: "GAAP diluted earnings per share of $2.59, up 63% and non-GAAP diluted earnings per share of $2.91, up 56%."
  • CFO Aujla said segment growth was led by Global Business Solutions: "GBS revenue grew 15% during the quarter, driven by Online Ecosystem, which grew 20%," and "Consumer segment... revenue grew 7%."
  • CFO Aujla reported Credit Karma and TurboTax growth rates and drivers: "Credit Karma revenue grew 9%, driven by personal loans and insurance," while "TurboTax revenue grew 1%" and "ProTax revenue grew 13%."
  • On capital allocation, CFO Aujla said, "We repurchased $1.5 billion of stock during the first quarter" and "The Board approved a quarterly dividend of $1.38 per share payable on January 15, 2027."

Q&A

  • Adam Wood, Morgan Stanley: Asked about the Credit Karma reset and tax monetization via Credit Karma; CEO Goodarzi: "First and foremost, nothing changes" and said "70% of the customers that came in through CK Tax were new to the franchise"; CFO Aujla: "we continue to be confident in the 3-year CAGRs... of 4% to 8%" for Consumer.
  • Brad Zelnick, Deutsche Bank: Asked what is cyclical vs. structural in Credit Karma and how to adapt; CEO Goodarzi cited "the demand growth rate slowing because of the interest rate changes" and "a shift... doing their discovery and their work in LLMs and AI platforms," adding "the impact was faster than we anticipated"; CFO Aujla said Intuit was "prudent" on fiscal 2027 assumptions for timing of cross-sell/LTV actions.
  • Taylor McGinnis, UBS: Asked why the model implies a second-half acceleration; CFO Aujla said it is "largely related to the TurboTax business" including mix shifts early in season and the refund-transfer recognition timing.
  • Aleksandr Zukin, Wolfe Research: Asked about QuickBooks demand/attach rates and AI-managed services; CEO Goodarzi said Intuit is "on the track that we expected to be" and added connected users show "higher adoption of services"; CFO Aujla pointed to accountant influence: "65% of our core QB customers have accountants" and "Over 70% of mid-market have accountants."
  • Sitikantha Panigrahi, Mizuho: Asked about assisted-category advertising and Sign and File pricing; CEO Goodarzi said "our growth engine is assisted tax" and highlighted local footprint expansion and that Sign and File targets customers who want "someone to own" accountability, adding Intuit will offer it "at a disruptive price point" (no specific price disclosed).
  • Sang-Jin Byun, Jefferies: Asked about the Q2 step-down and late-quarter slowing; CFO Aujla said Q2 reflects share actions in tax, refund-transfer timing shifting "$30 million" from Q2 to Q3, and Desktop normalization.
  • Rishi Jaluria, RBC: Asked whether proceeds from Mailchimp sale go fully to buybacks and how international strategy changes; CEO Goodarzi said the problem statement is unchanged but "our how completely changes" toward building capabilities in QuickBooks; CFO Aujla said, "Our intent is to use the entirety of the cash proceeds... to do buybacks in fiscal 2027."
  • Michael Turrin, Wells Fargo: Asked about Credit Karma telemetry and product response; CEO Goodarzi said the shift is "very limited to Credit Karma" and described work to "unlock" Credit Karma interactions so it is not "behind the firewall" for LLM discovery.
  • Samik Chatterjee, JPMorgan: Asked about behavior after QuickBooks Advanced pricing and about gross margin step-down; CEO Goodarzi said retention is "at 83%" and "within the control limits"; CFO Aujla said quarterly margin can move with marketing timing and that he was "very confident" in full-year margin commitments.

Sentiment analysis

  • Analysts: slightly negative, concentrated on Credit Karma’s guide reset and whether behavioral change is structural, with questions probing "how much... cyclical versus more structural" (Brad Zelnick, Deutsche Bank) and the implied second-half rebound.
  • Management: slightly positive in prepared remarks (partnerships, mid-market momentum, portfolio moves) but more defensive/explanatory in Q&A around Credit Karma, emphasizing "nothing changes" (CEO Goodarzi) and that the AI-driven discovery shift hit "faster than we anticipated" (CEO Goodarzi).
  • Versus last quarter, analysts shifted from broad AI disruption questions to near-term execution and demand sensitivity in Credit Karma, while management maintained confidence language such as "we continue to be confident" (CFO Aujla).

Quarter-over-quarter comparison

  • Portfolio/structure: Q1 included a new decision to divest Mailchimp ("signed an agreement to sell Mailchimp"), whereas Q4 discussed Mailchimp becoming a separate reportable segment in fiscal 2027.
  • Guidance tone: Q1 updated FY2027 total revenue growth to "8% to 9%" and narrowed the change to "limited to Credit Karma" (CFO Aujla); Q4 had set FY2027 at "9% to 10%" and expected Credit Karma growth of "11% to 13%."
  • Business emphasis: both quarters emphasized accelerating new customer growth and scaling Big Bets; Q1 added specific focus on Credit Karma placement in AI-powered discovery and highlighted new partnerships and MCP connector distribution.
  • Q&A focus: Q4 centered on whether FY2027 was a "bottom of the J curve" and pricing strategy risk in tax; Q1 centered on what drove Credit Karma’s underperformance and how quickly Intuit can adapt to LLM-driven discovery.

Risks and concerns

  • CFO Aujla said Credit Karma was pressured by "higher-than-expected interest rates" and "a shift in consumer behavior towards AI-powered experiences," and said Q2 guidance assumes "the demand environment remains at current levels."
  • CFO Aujla warned TurboTax Q2 revenue is expected "to be down year-over-year" due to deliberate price/value actions and the in-house refund transfer timing shift.
  • CEO Goodarzi said Credit Karma discovery dynamics changed faster than expected: "the impact was faster than we anticipated," and Intuit is applying TurboTax/QuickBooks playbooks to improve LLM visibility.

Final takeaway

Management framed Q1 as execution ahead of guidance alongside a set of strategy pivots with direct stock relevance: an agreement to sell Mailchimp, a FY2027 revenue outlook update attributed to Credit Karma trends, and tax-season actions expected to pressure near-term Consumer results (including a $30 million Q2-to-Q3 timing shift). Management repeatedly positioned adaptation to AI-driven discovery as central, while emphasizing continued momentum in Online Ecosystem and ongoing capital returns, including buybacks and a $1.38 quarterly dividend.

data.title: SunPower forecasts $61.8M Q4 revenue as it targets positive operating cash flow within next 2 quarters
data.description:
Earnings Call Insights: SunPower (SPWR) Q3 2026

Management View

  • CEO Thurman Rodgers framed Q3 as a rebound from execution issues, saying, "The headlines are quarter-on-quarter revenue is up $10.2 million, and our losses have been reduced by 3.3x (sic) [ 3.6x ]" (CEO & Executive Chairman Thurman Rodgers).
  • Rodgers said Q3 results were affected by non-cash cleanup items, noting, "That is a charge for old uncollectible AR" and adding GAAP operating income "contains 2 things: the AR write-off I just described and a $20 million goodwill impairment" (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).
  • Rodgers described cost actions and current staffing levels: "Our target is currently 700... we cut to 641" and added, "there are something like 40 to 50 headcount in the company that when we get truly lean, we will have to remove" (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).
  • Rodgers announced an accounting overhaul: "We have now retained Deloitte, a Big Four firm, and they're going to take over our accounting... BDO, we're going to leave alone, and we're going to have them work with Deloitte" (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).
  • Rodgers highlighted capital structure optics and the recent reverse split: "We just finished a reverse split, 35:1 reverse split... jumped up to its current $4 price" (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).
  • Commercial growth was positioned as a key expansion path. John Bergh said, "Our pipeline continues to build... that pipeline is growing to more than $25 million, and it's driving installation volume well into 2027 and beyond" (Executive Vice President of New Homes & Cobalt John Bergh).
  • A second growth vector was VPP. John McCranie said VPP offers "contribution margin of 40% versus 24% for classic TPO" and added, "Greenlight... has already done 200 VPP systems for SOLRITE through us" (John McCranie).
  • No CFO prepared remarks were included in this transcript; financial commentary was delivered by Rodgers and business updates by Bergh and McCranie.

Outlook

  • Rodgers guided Q4 revenue to "remain in the low 60s" and later specified, "the guidance is $61.8 million" (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).
  • Rodgers added profit expectations on a non-GAAP basis: "our goal is to cut in half" the non-GAAP operating loss from Q3 levels, and said the following quarter depends on Q1 conditions: "we don't know that yet" (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).
  • Versus the prior quarter’s posture, SunPower’s Q3 call shifted from Q2’s target of "$75 million or more" for Q3 revenue (Q2 call) to maintaining Q4 revenue in the low $60s, with added emphasis on commercial and VPP as incremental growth levers (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).

Financial Results

  • Rodgers reported, "I'm going to talk about the $65.1 million quarter with a $5 million loss" and clarified, "Our operating income was a loss of $4.9 million" on a non-GAAP basis (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).
  • Liquidity at quarter-end was described as, "Our cash at the end of the reported quarter was $13.1 million" (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).
  • Rodgers called out two major one-time, non-cash items affecting GAAP results: "a charge for old uncollectible AR" and "a $20 million goodwill impairment" (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).

Q&A

  • Derek Soderberg, Cantor Fitzgerald: asked about growth capacity and whether capital could limit acceleration; CEO Rodgers replied, "right now, capital is not limiting us" and said the constraint is operational execution: "Our limitation on growth is... we have to make the machine run faster" (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).
  • Soderberg, Cantor Fitzgerald: asked whether more cleanup charges are likely and how confident management is in the remaining backlog; Rodgers said he expects "another round" of AR write-offs in the year-end 10-K, adding, "It won't be as big... but it will be noncash and it won't matter" (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).
  • Sioban Hickie (web/inbound question): asked about inbound vs outbound demand; Rodgers answered, "It's all door knocking" and said SunPower laid off its virtual sales force because it "costs more dollars per job" than 1099s (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).
  • Hickie (web/inbound question): asked about positive operating cash flow timing; Rodgers responded, "Within the next 2 quarters" (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).
  • Hickie (web/inbound question): asked whether management or the company might buy shares; Rodgers said, "in my own case... I have 50 million shares and $111 million in it" (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).

Sentiment Analysis

  • Analyst tone was neutral-to-slightly positive, with Soderberg linking multiple initiatives and asking, "if we're going to return to growth, what's sort of your capacity for growth here today?" (Derek Soderberg, Cantor Fitzgerald).
  • Management tone mixed operational candor with forward-leaning confidence. Rodgers said, "the loss is unacceptable" while also stating, "right now, capital is not limiting us" and setting a cash-flow timeline of "Within the next 2 quarters" (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).
  • Compared with Q2, management appeared less defensive on liquidity and more focused on process controls (Deloitte engagement) and execution accountability, while acknowledging further non-cash cleanup may continue (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).

Quarter-over-Quarter Comparison

  • In Q2, the company characterized results as a "disaster revenue quarter" (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers, Q2 call) and guided Q3 to "$75 million or more" and operating loss to "less than $1 million" (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers, Q2 call); in Q3, Rodgers emphasized "misexecuted in Q2 of 2026" and re-centered guidance on Q4 in "the low 60s" (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).
  • Strategy emphasis broadened in Q3: Rodgers highlighted two growth vectors explicitly—"commercial" and "virtual power plants"—to move beyond the "$65 million a quarter" residential base (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).
  • Analyst focus in Q2 leaned heavily on cash tightness and backlog conversion; in Q3, questions shifted toward scalability, capital access in an acceleration scenario, and confidence in cleanup cadence (Derek Soderberg, Cantor Fitzgerald).

Risks and Concerns

  • Rodgers flagged continued accounting complexity and legacy cleanups, stating, "SunPower's accounting has never met the zero-defect standards" and anticipating an additional year-end AR cleanup cycle (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).
  • Execution risk remained central. Rodgers said Q2 underperformance resulted from quality and management problems, and warned future misses would again be execution-driven: "if we don't [hit the forecast], it will be an execution problem" (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).
  • Seasonal headwinds were acknowledged with Q4 described as the "winter quarter" for a nationwide footprint, though the company still guided to remain in the low $60s (CEO & Executive Chairman Rodgers).

Final Takeaway

Rodgers said SunPower’s Q3 reflected a recovery from Q2 execution issues, with results impacted by non-cash AR write-offs and a $20 million goodwill impairment, while management moved to tighten controls by bringing in Deloitte. For Q4, Rodgers guided revenue to $61.8 million and set a non-GAAP goal to cut the operating loss roughly in half, while describing commercial (including a $25 million pipeline) and VPP (including higher stated contribution margins and early multi-state expansion) as the two primary growth vectors intended to move the company beyond the mid-$60 million quarterly residential base and toward positive operating cash flow "within the next 2 quarters."

data.title: Decline in U.S. diesel prices likely to continue, Energy Secretary says
data.description:
U.S. diesel prices should continue to decline from record highs as refined products from the Persian Gulf return to the market and unsanctioned Russian diesel adds to downward pressure on prices, U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright said Thursday.

"The trajectory we're on right now is downward for the foreseeable future," although the path depends on nothing "big or bad" happening, Wright told The Wall Street Journal in an interview at the Partnership for Transatlantic Energy Cooperation conference in Warsaw.

Even as no Russian diesel has actually arrived in the U.S. and several fuel tankers have shifted course after struggling to find American buyers willing to accept the cargoes, Wright said the return of the country’s fuel to the global market puts downward pressure on the price U.S. consumers pay at the pump.

The national average price of diesel hit an all-time high of $6.53/gal in September, according to AAA, but prices have since eased to $5.93 on Thursday, while remaining well above the $3.78/gal average price from a year ago.

Wright also said U.S. diesel prices would never have risen into the $6.50s if European allies had been more proactive in releasing fuel from strategic reserves to the market.

Europe was "remarkably reluctant to release their diesel stores despite their promises to do so," Wright said, which "led to prices going higher than they should have gone."

Crude oil futures finished flat in a choppy session Thursday as tensions in the Middle East continued to be offset by improving supply.

"The oil market has become acclimated to periodic flare-ups, just as long as there is no return to all-out war," Raymond James strategist Pavel Molchanov said in a note. "With oil production among OPEC's Persian Gulf members having reached 87% of pre-war levels, the industry is gradually adapting."

A broader retreat across commodity markets and a stronger U.S. dollar are also weighing on sentiment, creating additional headwinds, analysts said.

Meanwhile, the International Energy Agency said prolonged disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz could substantially reduce the world's reliance on the waterway over the next decade as Middle Eastern producers develop alternative export routes.

Front-month Nymex crude (CL1:COM) for December delivery fell less than 0.1% to $83.21/bbl, while front-month Brent crude (CO1:COM) for January delivery gained less than 0.1% to $91.98/bbl, and front-month Nymex natural gas (NG1:COM) for December delivery dipped 3.1% to $3.268/MMBtu.
